title: Enable GTM/cookie tracking on p3m.dev and packagemanager.posit.co
description:
## What

Adds `packagemanager.posit.co` and `p3m.dev` to the hostname allowlist in `_extensions/posit-docs/assets/_analytics.html`, for both:

- the Google Tag Manager (`GTM-KHBDBW7`) script injection, and
- the OneTrust cookie preference center icon in the footer

This matches the existing `docs.posit.co` / `netlify.app` behavior. (`includes("p3m.dev")` also covers `*.p3m.dev` staging hosts.)

## Why

Posit Package Manager vendors this theme and serves the docs under `p3m.dev/__docs__` and `packagemanager.posit.co/__docs__`. Because the analytics snippet only activates on `docs.posit.co`/`netlify.app`, **no GA4 data is collected for the PPM-hosted docs**, even though the rest of those sites track fine. Reported in rstudio/package-manager#16379.

## ⚠️ Cookie-consent / WebOps gate

The README notes that cookie consent is managed by GTM and that **WebOps must opt a site into tracking** before the theme is bumped to enable it. This PR is the code half; it should not be released/merged until `p3m.dev` and `packagemanager.posit.co` are confirmed opted into GTM tracking. Flagging so the compliance step isn't skipped.

## Follow-ups for maintainers

- `changelog.md` entry + version bump on the next release (left to your release process).
- Once released, PPM will re-vendor the extension to pick this up.

## Testing

After a site is opted in and the theme is deployed, load `https://p3m.dev/__docs__/` and confirm the `GTM-KHBDBW7` container loads (GA4 real-time) and the cookie preference icon appears in the footer; verify `docs.posit.co` behavior is unchanged.

title: fix: tweak selector logic to hide cookie icon in a more accessible way
description:
## Description
This PR tweaks the JS we're using to hide the cookie icon when docs are hosted on domains where we don't include GTM, and hides the containing `<li>` instead of its children. This allows a screenreader to properly calculate the length of the list of items in the footer.

Fixes #102 

## Verification

- [X] Brought up VoiceOver (cmd + fn + F5) and then the rotor (ctrl + option + u) to navigate to the footer, then moved to the list containing the items (ctrl + option + right arrow until it's selected). Confirmed that when the cookie icon is hidden, the length of the list announced is accurate
- [X] Brought up VoiceOver (cmd + fn + F5) and then the rotor (ctrl + option + u) to navigate to the footer, then moved to the list containing the items (ctrl + option + right arrow until it's selected). Confirmed that when the cookie icon is visible, the length of the list announced is also accurate.

title: Release 8.1.3
description: Sets up the `8.1.3` release.

title: Raise Mermaid contrast to meet WCAG AA in both color modes
description:
Quarto's Mermaid defaults render node labels in `$primary` on an `rgba($primary, 0.1)` fill - the same hue on itself. Node label on node fill measures 4.59:1 in light mode and 4.22:1 in dark, the latter below the WCAG AA floor of 4.5:1. Diagrams are often scaled down to fit the text column, which makes it worse.

Both themes now pin opaque node fills and label colors from the Posit palette, with the measured ratios in comments:

| Node label on node fill | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Light mode | 4.59:1 | 8.12:1 |
| Dark mode | 4.22:1 | 7.65:1 |

Three smaller items ride along:

- `--mermaid-font-weight` is now set. Quarto's Mermaid CSS reads the custom property but never emits it, so the declaration resolved to nothing.
- Edge labels get the page background as a pill rather than a Posit-blue fill, which only reached 4.6:1 against `$body-color`.
- `.cluster rect` gets a `stroke-width`, so subgraph borders stay visible when a diagram is scaled down.

These have been running in the Posit Connect docs since posit-dev/connect#42597. Lifting them into the theme means every product picks them up and Connect can drop its local modification of the vendored extension, which currently has to be re-applied by hand on every upgrade. Tracked by posit-dev/connect#42711.

The second commit takes up the review point about the changelog. `changelog.md` gets an `Unreleased` section holding this change, and the README asks pull requests to write their entry there rather than leaving the release to reconstruct it from the commit log. The release step becomes renaming that heading. Still no version bump here; that stays with the release pull request.

## Validation

`quarto preview`, then the "Mermaids" section of the index page in both light and dark mode. The flowchart there covers subgraphs and an edge label; node fills should be opaque rather than a wash, and no label should sit light-on-light in dark mode.

`changelog.md` is excluded from the render, so the doc changes do not affect the site.
